Transferring  P rom th e D epartment  of  
Agriculture  to the  D epartment  of 
Commerce  C ertain  L ands at S itka , 
Alaska, for U se as a M agnetic  and 
Seismological  O bservatory  S it e by 
the  B ureau of C oast and G eodetic  
Survey
WHEREAS by Executive order of Au­
gust 12, 1898, certain lands in the Ter­
ritory of Alaska were reserved and set  
apart as an agricultural experiment sta­
tion for the use of the United States De­
partment of Agriculture; and  
WHEREAS the Department of Agri­
culture no longer requires the said lands  
for use as an experimental station and  
has abandoned such use of the lands;  
and
WHEREAS it appears that reservation  
of such lands for the use of the United  
States Coast and Geodetic Survey, De­
partment of Commerce, as a magnetic  
and seismological observatory site would  
be in the public interest:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by the act of  
June 25, 1910, c. 421, 36 Stat. 847, as  
amended by the act of August 24, 1912,  
c. 569, 37 Stat. 497, the said Executive  
order of August 12, 1898, is hereby re­
voked, and the lands described therein  
are hereby reserved and set apart for the  
use of the United States Coast and Geo­
detic Survey, Department of Commerce,  
as a magnetic and seismological observa­
tory site.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 8168 (4 FR 2415, June 14, 1939): it recites that the Agriculture Department abandoned its Sitka, Alaska experiment-station reservation, revokes the Executive order of Aug. 12, 1898, and reserves those lands for the Coast and Geodetic Survey (Commerce) as a magnetic and seismological observatory site. It is a single operative sentence with no own term and no savings clause. I read the complete held EO 8854 (6 FR 4181, Aug. 16, 1941), titled 'Revoking Executive Order No. 8168 of June 14, 1939, and Withdrawing the Land Released Thereby and Other Land ...': para. 1 orders that Executive Order No. 8168 'is hereby revoked', with no condition, exception or savings language, and para. 2 separately withdraws and reserves the same lands plus an adjoining tract for the same Survey use under the President's own authority. Para. 2 is a new reservation made by EO 8854, not a continuation of EO 8168, so the whole of EO 8168 is ended by para. 1. The catalog line 'Revoked by: EO 8854' and the empty 1989 snapshot agree, but the basis is the held acting text. D6 self-check: history lists only the EO 8854 revocation events; a text search of the held corpus finds EO 8168 named only in EO 8854, in EO 8169 and EO 8853 (copies of the same Federal Register pages) and in page indexes of unrelated volumes (OCR page-number hits), so no later order amends, revives or extends EO 8168, and no earlier ending exists in the held record. Provisional NO hypothesis only.

Held EO 8854 para. 1: 'Executive Order No. 8168 of June 14, 1939 ... is hereby revoked'; para. 2 makes a new, separate withdrawal of the same and adjoining lands under its own authority. My status NO (8168 itself ended; the reservation continues under 8854). D6: other hits (8169, 8853, 8855, 8856) are copies of the same FR pages; no later order names 8168. Accept.

versions.research_rationale:
I read the complete held Federal Register original of Executive Order 8168 (4 FR 2415, June 16, 1939; signed June 14, 1939). After recitals that the Department of Agriculture no longer needed and had abandoned its Sitka, Alaska experiment-station lands, a single operative sentence revokes the Executive order of August 12, 1898 and reserves the lands for the Coast and Geodetic Survey of the Department of Commerce as a magnetic and seismological observatory site. It has no duration, condition or savings language. I read the complete held Federal Register text of Executive Order 8854 (6 FR 4181, August 20, 1941; signed August 16, 1941), titled as revoking Executive Order 8168. The Federal Register text layer renders the order number in the quotation as 81681 (a footnote mark run into the number); the actual checker reads that as a different order and reports a mechanical order-exists failure, which is an extraction artifact. An American Presidency Project transcription of the same order is held and agrees in substance, but an official copy is held, so the transcription may not be used as the quoted source. Paragraph 1 orders that Executive Order No. 8168 of June 14, 1939, is revoked, with no condition or exception. Paragraph 2 separately withdraws the lands contained in the 8168 reservation and an adjoining tract for the same Survey use under the President's own authority. Paragraph 2 is a new reservation made by Executive Order 8854, not a continuation of Executive Order 8168, so the whole of Executive Order 8168 ended on August 16, 1941. I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them: the U.S. Code search (through 2026-10-09) and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) found no citation of this order, and the Federal Register disposition-note search found only the revocation by Executive Order 8854 (two catalog entries for the same event). The Federal Register text layer is machine extracted and was checked only as text; the page images were not inspected.
